For each prime factor \(p \in \{5,13,31\}\), since \(p\mid n(n+1)\), we must have either
\[
n\equiv 0 \pmod p \quad \text{or} \quad n\equiv -1 \pmod p.
\]
These choices are mutually exclusive, so there are \(2^3=8\) possible assignments. By CRT, each assignment gives exactly one residue class modulo \(2015\). Since \(n\) runs from \(1\) to \(2015\), each residue class occurs exactly once.

Thus the number of such \(S_n\) is
\[
\boxed{8}.
\]
